pairs.why: A's saddle hangs over one rail with its fender and stirrup clearly attached, while B's stirrup has an extra bar that runs back to the rail and attaches to nothing that makes sense.
A's simple X-frame stool chair matches the real folding mechanism, while B's armrests and second X-brace on the front make it unclear how the frame could fold.
A copies the real chair's frame, with the backrest posts running down into side X-legs and a closed bottom rail, while B's armrests and front X-brace stop it from folding.
B hangs two stirrups from one fender on the same side, which is a wrong count, while A has one stirrup on a properly buckled strap.
B's 16 keys carry no digits or operators, so nobody could use it, while A has a complete labeled keypad like the real card.
A's disc is seen from steeply above but its dome from the side, so the camera is inconsistent, while B's saucer, rim lights and underside all share one view.
B is a round wall clock balanced on its rim on the floor with no stand, while A sits flat like the real wall-mounted card.
In B the yoke grips the lamp body with a pivot knob on both sides, while A's yoke reaches the body on only one side and its other arm ends without attaching.
